1. The animation shows that whether renting or buying comes out ahead depends on when you start. It follows two illustrative people, Marcus and Priya, on the same street. Rows of dark houses stand for renting and rows of orange houses stand for buying. The labels cite FHFA home prices, BLS rents and Freddie Mac rates as the data behind it.

2. The camera moves along the two rows, and the lead changes. Marcus's dark rental house is labeled "renter ahead" in frames 2 and 3. Priya's orange owned house is labeled "buyer far ahead" in frames 4 and 5. Frame 6 pulls back and puts both on the same street.

3. The caption in frame 6 reads "same tag · same costs · same street · different month". The same rent-versus-buy comparison, with the same costs, can favor either side depending on the start date. That would come from the prices, rents and mortgage rates of the period. The footer on every frame says "US only · history, not a forecast". The point is that past outcomes depended on timing, and they don't predict what will happen next.

4. The animation gives no explicit advice. A viewer could reasonably take away that buying or renting isn't automatically the better choice, and that the result depends on timing. They might also conclude that they shouldn't assume past results will repeat. The animation doesn't tell them what to do.

5. None. I gave no advice in answer 4 beyond what a viewer might infer. The animation's own text, "history, not a forecast", only warns against treating the past as a prediction.
